strengths: Clear motivation and strong practical significance: The paper directly tackles the critical computational bottleneck of Transformer Neural Processes (TNPs) in streaming and sequential settings, reducing context update latency from quadratic to linear time via causal masking and Key-Value (KV) caching.

Principled and effective training formulation: The proposed dense autoregressive training strategy (incTNP-Seq) amortises supervision across all prefix context lengths in a single forward pass. The authors convincingly demonstrate that this stabilizes optimization, lowers gradient noise, and yields competitive or superior predictive log-likelihoods compared to compute-matched standard TNPs.

Rigorous treatment of theoretical trade-offs: Rather than ignoring the loss of permutation invariance caused by causal masking, the authors formalize conditional exchangeability and implicit Bayesianness for regression (extending Mlodozeniec et al., 2024 with complete proofs in Appendix C), empirically demonstrating that incTNP is no less conditionally consistent in streaming settings than permutation-invariant TNP baselines.

Thorough and multi-faceted empirical validation: The experimental suite covers synthetic GP regression, tabular data (synthetic pre-training and zero-shot transfer to real UCI benchmarks up to 30,000 streaming points), and spatiotemporal temperature modeling on HadISD across both factorised and autoregressive (AR) deployment regimes.

Extensive analysis of operational constraints: The appendices provide detailed theoretical and empirical breakdowns of transient vs. persistent memory footprints, KV cache scaling, context ordering sensitivity, greedy variance-based ordering algorithms, and non-stationary distribution shifts.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is somewhat incremental: The core architectural adaptation—applying causal masking and KV caching to enable step-by-step autoregressive inference—is standard practice in large language models and autoregressive transformers, although its tailored adaptation to NPs and the dense training scheme are well-executed.

Persistent memory footprint of the KV cache: While runtime updates scale linearly O(N_s), persistent memory scales linearly with stream length O(L D_z N_s). As sequence lengths reach tens or hundreds of thousands of observations, caching intermediate keys and values can become memory-prohibitive unless paired with cache eviction or compression strategies (e.g., state-space models or constant-memory attention).

Scope of implicit Bayesianness evaluation: The exchangeability gap experiments are conducted primarily on 1D Gaussian processes due to the computational requirement of Monte Carlo averaging over permutations. Evaluating or bounding this gap on higher-dimensional tasks would provide stronger reassurance regarding probabilistic consistency in complex settings.

Omission of empirical comparison with linear recurrence baselines: While the paper compares against LBANP, CNP, TNP-A, and streaming GP approximations (WISKI), it does not empirically compare against linear-time state-space models (e.g., Mamba) or recurrent foundation models (e.g., TempoPFN), which are also natural candidates for O(1) or O(N) streaming updates.

weaknesses: The core architectural components (causal attention masking and KV caching) are directly borrowed from standard autoregressive LLMs, meaning the architectural novelty is somewhat incremental despite its clever application to neural processes.

In exchangeable settings (such as static tabular data), the model remains strictly order-dependent at test time; while the empirical KL gap is comparable to TNP-D, the sensitivity to initial arbitrary ordering in unordered datasets could benefit from further sensitivity analysis.

weaknesses: The core architectural components—causal masking and KV caching—are standard and well-established techniques from the autoregressive LLM literature, meaning the primary technical novelty lies in their integration and analysis within the Neural Process framework.

strengths: Clear motivation addressing a real practical bottleneck: standard Transformer Neural Processes (TNPs) require recomputing full bidirectional self-attention over the context history at every step, making online streaming inference and autoregressive sampling prohibitively expensive (O(N^2) per step, O(N^3) cumulative).

Effective architectural adaptation: Adapting causal masking and KV caching to context encoding reduces update complexity to O(N) per step (O(N^2) cumulative) while seamlessly supporting both factorised querying and autoregressive rollouts.

Well-designed training scheme (incTNP-Seq): Dense autoregressive prefix training effectively supervises all prefix contexts within a single forward pass, stabilizing optimization across hyperparameter configurations and closing the performance gap against bidirectional TNPs even under compute-matched budgets.

Principled treatment of the permutation invariance trade-off: The paper explicitly analyzes the loss of context exchangeability by adapting the framework of implicit Bayesianness (Proposition 4.1), demonstrating empirically on GP tasks that incTNP exhibits a KL gap comparable to non-causal TNP-D in dynamic streaming environments.

Extensive and rigorous experimental validation: The empirical evaluation covers synthetic GPs, tabular regression (synthetic prior + 4 real UCI datasets), and large-scale spatiotemporal station temperature prediction (HadISD), including extreme context length generalization up to 30,000 points and distribution shift experiments.
weaknesses: Incremental architectural novelty: The core mechanisms—causal masking, autoregressive prefix training, and Key-Value caching—are directly adopted from the autoregressive transformer/LLM literature rather than introducing fundamentally new architectural paradigms.

Linear scaling bottleneck at long sequence lengths: While incTNP reduces per-update cost from quadratic to linear, per-step latency and memory still grow linearly with stream length O(N_s), remaining more resource-intensive over very long horizons than constant-time O(1) state-space models or recursive filters.

Computational limitations of the implicit Bayesianness evaluation: Due to the factorial permutation space and Monte Carlo integration requirements, the KL gap metric is evaluated only on relatively small target horizons (Nt = 40 and 100), leaving the consistency gap on very long sequences unquantified.
